# haxe.run

> A Haxe and hx+ playground that compiles and runs code entirely in the browser tab.
> There is no build server: the compiler (hxc) is WebAssembly running on the page.
> Everything the editor can do is also available programmatically through
> `window.haxeRun`, so programs and AI agents are first-class consumers.

## Start here

- The API is `window.haxeRun`, available on https://haxe.run after the page loads.
- Call `haxeRun.help()` for a printable summary, or `haxeRun.schema()` for a
  machine-readable description of every method, option, and result shape.
- Full reference: [AGENTS.md](/AGENTS.md)

## Minimum useful example

```js
await haxeRun.ready();

const r = await haxeRun.run({
  files: { "Main.hx": 'class Main { static function main() { trace("hi"); } }' }
});

r.ok;      // true
r.stdout;  // "Main.hx:1: hi"
```

## What to know before calling it

- Every method returns a Promise. Await `haxeRun.ready()` once before the first
  call; the compiler is ~9 MB compressed and takes a few seconds to boot.
- `compile()` and `run()` are stateless. Pass `files`, get a result. They do not
  read or disturb whatever a human has open in the editor.
- Failures resolve, they do not reject. Check `ok`, then read `errors`, which are
  structured objects with `file`, `line`, `column`, and `message`, so code can be
  repaired without parsing prose.
- `files` maps path to source: `{ "Main.hx": "...", "geom/Shape.hx": "..." }`.
  Subdirectories are package paths.
- The entry point is inferred (the module with `static function main`, preferring
  `Main.hx`). Override with `main`.
- Libraries come from a `build.hxml` entry in `files`: `-lib feathersui` for one
  haxe.run serves, or `-lib name:git:https://github.com/owner/repo#tag` for any
  haxelib on GitHub. See the Libraries section of AGENTS.md.
- Importing `openfl.*` automatically builds an OpenFL/Lime html5 app. These
  compiles take appreciably longer than plain Haxe and render to a canvas rather
  than printing to stdout.

## The loop this is built for

Generate Haxe, compile it, read structured diagnostics, repair, repeat. `run()`
does the whole cycle in one call and hands back captured console output, so a
model can verify its own code rather than guessing.

## Language

- hx+ is a strict superset of Haxe 4.3: valid Haxe is valid hx+.
- The compiler is hxc, a faithful Haxe 4.3 compiler written in Haxe.
- Details: https://hxplus.org
